content.title: What are Generics?
content.description: Generics allow classes, interfaces, and methods to operate on different data types while providing compile-time type safety and eliminating unnecessary type casting.

content.content: Before Java introduced Generics, collections stored objects as Object, requiring explicit type casting when retrieving elements. Generics enable developers to specify the data type while creating collections or classes, making code safer, cleaner, and easier to maintain.

content.title: Why Use Generics?
content.content: Generics improve type safety, reduce runtime errors, eliminate explicit casting, and make code reusable across multiple data types.
Generic Classes
A generic class uses a type parameter (commonly T) that is replaced with an actual type when an object is created.

content.title: Generic Class Example
Key Idea
content.description: The type parameter T acts as a placeholder and is replaced by an actual type during object creation.

content.content: Generic Methods
Generic methods work independently of generic classes and allow methods to operate on different data types.

content.title: Generic Method Example
Compile-Time Safety
content.content: Generics detect incompatible data types during compilation instead of allowing runtime ClassCastException.
Generic Collections
Collections such as ArrayList, HashSet, and HashMap commonly use generics to ensure they store only the intended data type.

content.title: Generic Collection Example

content.content: Multiple Type Parameters
Generic classes can declare multiple type parameters when working with more than one data type.

content.title: Multiple Type Parameters

Generics vs Non-Generics
Bounded Generics
Bounded type parameters restrict the types that can be used with generics. For example, <T extends Number> allows only numeric types.

content.content: Applications

items.question: Collections Framework
items.answer: ArrayList, HashMap, HashSet, Queue, and other collections use generics extensively.

items.question: Reusable Libraries
items.answer: Develop generic utility classes that work with multiple data types.

items.question: Framework Development
items.answer: Spring, Hibernate, and many Java frameworks use generics for type-safe APIs.

items.question: Custom Data Structures
items.answer: Implement reusable stacks, queues, trees, and linked lists.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Reusable Storage Box
content.content: Imagine a storage box labeled with the type of item it can hold, such as books or toys. A generic class works the same way—it accepts only the specified type, preventing accidental placement of incompatible items.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interview questions frequently cover type parameters, generic classes, generic methods, bounded types, wildcards, type erasure, and the advantages of generics over non-generic code.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Can primitive data types be used directly as generic types?
items.answer: No. Use wrapper classes such as Integer, Double, and Character.

items.question: Are generics available at runtime?
items.answer: No. Java uses type erasure, so generic type information is removed during compilation.

items.question: Should raw types be used instead of generic types?
items.answer: No. Raw types disable compile-time type checking and reduce type safety.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Generics provide compile-time type safety, reusable code, and eliminate unnecessary casting while working with different data types.
